key_insight: Minimum dissipation in driven stationary systems and maximum dissipation during frozen-state relaxation arise from the same convex, minimized Rayleighian framework.
engineering_relevance: The framework clarifies how variational formulations can recover dissipative flow equations while accounting for energy transport and inertia.
method: Analyze thermodynamic extremal properties across stationary and relaxation regimes.
Use Reynolds transport to formulate continuum energy rates and hold inertial driving forces fixed during variation.
Switch to material coordinates for Navier–Stokes flow to remove the explicit convective acceleration term.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical tests on Stokes, unsteady Stokes, Navier–Stokes flow, and dissipative Lagrangian mechanics, but no numerical benchmarks or experimental data.
watch_item: With inertia, an extremal statement requires the frozen driving force to be independent of the varied rate, demanding careful choices of variables and coordinates.
paper_title: Variational principles for dissipative continua: transport theorems, inertia, and the minimum-maximum duality
